Lemon Connect Cameroon

An interactive laboratory on why Internet access in Cameroon is slow and costly. It models the path of a packet from a handset in Douala to a server, from radio access and power supply to the backbone, international transit and market structure, and every figure on screen is dated and sourced.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem statement

Most users in Cameroon live with slow and expensive connections without knowing where the constraint lies: the cell, its power supply, the backbone, the international link or the market itself. Public debate often blames a single actor without evidence, and the available data are scattered across reports in two languages.

02

Contribution

The platform turns the network into experiments. On the home page a request from a phone in Douala crosses each item of equipment, and the visitor can induce congestion, a power cut or a fibre cut and watch throughput and latency respond. A 4G and 5G laboratory locates the bottleneck in a cell, and a fault laboratory of sixteen incidents shows wrong repairs failing. Further modules assign technical, contractual and regulatory responsibility, model the market under nine scenarios and a two-operator game, compare satellite and terrestrial links, size an installation, simulate building an operator over five years and propose a policy roadmap for ART and MINPOSTEL. An observatory, ten courses, an atlas of cables and of the CAMIX exchange point, and a sources page complete it.

03

Architecture

React and TypeScript with Vite and Tailwind, Zustand for application state and d3-geo for cartography. The simulations run on a small TypeScript engine tested on its own. A welcome screen offers four paths, every page has a guided tour, and technical terms show their definition on hover or tap; citizen and engineer modes adjust the depth of explanation.

04

Method and data

The engine implements radio capacity following the 3GPP model, queueing, fibre propagation delay, power availability, a market model with fixed costs, a game between two operators and a five-year financial model. Facts are maintained in two research files totalling more than 100 dated sources, and each figure on screen carries its reference.

05

Verification and limitations

52 unit tests verify the engine and 54 browser tests traverse the site on a desktop and an Android phone. Simulations are labelled as teaching models: they illustrate mechanisms and are not measurements of the operators’ networks.
